flawed_step: Lines 0116-0130 (step (iii)): the claim that 's has no net inflow', hence |f| = sum_{y:(s->y) in E} f(s,y), |g| = sum_{y:(s->y) in E} g(s,y), and therefore |g|-|f| = sum_{y:(s->y) in E} [g(s,y)-f(s,y)]. This drops every original edge directed INTO s, whose residual backward arcs (s,y) carry h-flow out of s. The stated justification confuses 'no NET inflow' (a triviality at s under the net-value definition) with 'no inflow at all' (an extra hypothesis never granted).
counterexample:
G: vertices s, a, b, c, t. Edges and capacities: (s,a) c=10, (a,t) c=10, (s,b) c=1, (b,c) c=1, (c,s) c=1. (No antiparallel pairs; every intermediate vertex conserves.)

Flow f: f(s,a)=1, f(a,t)=1, f(s,b)=1, f(b,c)=1, f(c,s)=1, feasible (each within capacity); conservation holds at a (in 1, out 1), b (in 1, out 1), c (in 1, out 1). Value |f| = net outflow of s = [f(s,a)+f(s,b)] - f(c,s) = (1+1) - 1 = 1, matching the net inflow at t, which is 1.

Flow g: g(s,a)=5, g(a,t)=5, all other edges 0. Feasible; conservation holds at a, b, c. |g| = 5 - 0 = 5. So |g| > |f|, as the hypothesis requires.

Now apply the proof's step (iii) verbatim:
  Proof asserts |f| = sum_{y:(s->y) in E} f(s,y) = f(s,a) + f(s,b) = 1 + 1 = 2.
  Truth: |f| = 1. FALSE (2 != 1).

And the displayed consequence on lines 0127-0130:
  Proof asserts |g| - |f| = sum_{y:(s->y) in E} [g(s,y) - f(s,y)] = (5-1) + (0-1) = 4 + (-1) = 3.
  Truth: |g| - |f| = 5 - 1 = 4. FALSE (3 != 4).

The missing amount is exactly the edge (c,s) into s: since g(c,s)=0 < f(c,s)=1, the proof's own construction puts h = f(c,s) - g(c,s) = 1 on the BACKWARD residual arc (s,c), which leaves s and must be counted in the net outflow of h at s. Indeed the correct h is h(s,a)=4, h(a,t)=4, h(b,s)=1 (backward arc of (s,b)), h(c,b)=1 (backward arc of (b,c)), h(s,c)=1 (backward arc of (c,s)), giving net outflow at s = 4 + 1 - 1 = 4 = |g| - |f|. So the theorem itself is true here, but the equation the proof uses to establish |h| = |g| - |f| evaluates to 3, not 4, and the intermediate identity |f| = sum of f out of s is off by 1. The chain from line 0118 to line 0158 therefore does not go through.
reasoning_summary: The construction h = (g-f) on forward residual arcs / (f-g) on backward residual arcs is the standard one, and parts (i) and (ii) survive a first pass. The riskiest concrete claim is in part (iii), where the proof replaces the value of a flow (net outflow at s) with the plain sum of flow on edges leaving s, justified by the slogan 's has no net inflow'. That is only legitimate if G has no edges entering s. Building a network with a flow-carrying cycle s -> b -> c -> s makes f route 1 unit around that cycle: the proof's formula reports |f| = 2 when |f| = 1, and reports |g| - |f| = 3 when the true difference is 4. The omitted unit is precisely the backward residual arc (s,c) generated by the edge (c,s), which the proof's own definition of h charges with 1 unit of outflow from s. Since step (iii) is the step that establishes the value claim in the theorem, the proof as written is invalid. (A second, independent break: line 0063's identity g(x,y)-f(x,y) = h(x,y)-h(y,x) is self-contradictory when G contains antiparallel edges (u,v) and (v,u) -- applying it to both arcs and adding forces g(u,v)-f(u,v) + g(v,u)-f(v,u) = 0, false e.g. for f(u,v)=5, g(u,v)=2, f(v,u)=0, g(v,u)=1 -- and h is not even well defined there, since the arc name (v,u) receives both 3 and 1.)
